text: At that time the LORD said to me, "Cut for yourself two stone tablets like the first ones and come up to me on the mountain. Also make yourself a wooden chest.

versions.text: At that time the LORD said to me, "Cut two stone tablets like the first ones and come up to me on the mountain. Also make yourself a wooden chest.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has the reflexive 'לְךָ' with both commands ('cut for yourself... make for yourself'), which the translation renders only in the second clause. Including it in both preserves the parallel structure of the divine command.

text: I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you smashed, and you shall put them in the chest."
So I made a chest of acacia wood, cut two stone tablets like the first ones, and went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hand.

versions.text: So I made a chest of acacia wood, cut two stone tablets like the first ones, and went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hands.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has the singular 'בְּיָדִי' (in my hand). The singular is also the customary rendering and keeps the rhythm of the clause.

text: And he wrote on the tablets, in the same writing as before, the Ten Commandments that the LORD had spoken to you on the mountain out of the fire on the day of the assembly. Then the LORD gave them to me.
I turned and came down from the mountain and put the tablets in the chest I had made—and there they remain, as the LORD commanded me.
Now the Israelites set out from Beeroth Bene-jaakan to Moserah. There Aaron died and there he was buried, and his son Eleazar became priest in his place.
From there they traveled to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land of flowing streams.
At that time the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to stand before the LORD to serve him, and to pronounce blessings in his name, as they do to this day.
That is why Levi has no share or inheritance alongside his brothers; the LORD himself is his inheritance, as the LORD your God told him.
I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights, as I had before, and once again the LORD listened to me; he was unwilling to destroy you.
And the LORD said to me, "Get up, set out at the head of the people, so that they may go in and take possession of the land I swore to their fathers to give them."
And now, Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you but to fear the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, to love him, and to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
and to keep the commandments and statutes of the LORD that I am giving you today for your own good?
See, to the LORD your God belong the heavens and the highest heavens, the earth and everything in it.
Yet it was on your fathers that the LORD set his heart in love, and he chose you, their descendants after them, out of all the peoples—as it is this day.
So circumcise your hearts, and stiffen your necks no longer.

versions.text: So circumcise your hearts, and be stubborn no longer.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew idiom 'ערפכם לא תקשו' (do not harden your neck) is vivid and is echoed elsewhere in Deuteronomy; 'be stubborn' flattens the image. Keeping the neck imagery preserves the poetic parallel with 'circumcise your hearts' and reads well aloud.

text: For the LORD your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great God, mighty and awesome, who shows no partiality and takes no bribe.
He secures justice for the orphan and the widow, and he loves the foreigner, giving him food and clothing.
You too must love the foreigner, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
Fear the LORD your God; serve him, hold fast to him, and swear by his name.
He is your praise, and he is your God, who did for you these great and awesome things that you saw with your own eyes.
Your fathers went down to Egypt seventy persons strong, and now the LORD your God has made you as numerous as the stars in the sky.
